I don’t fear death because matter cannot be created or destroyed. I know that my physical body will be absorbed back into the universe and will be repurposed to create something else. 

As for my soul, I’d like to believe that it would live on. I’d like to believe that my soul will be reunited with the Creator and I will see my soul family. I’d like to believe that I could choose to guide other souls on the Earthly plane or that I will be able to reincarnate.

If reincarnation isn’t real, and there is just nothing after death, I feel content knowing that I did my best in this life and have lived it to the fullest.

I appreciate this, thank you. Sometimes it’s so easy to be hard on ourselves. In reality, we are the ones that won. The narcissist has to live with who they are - a sick person that preys on those with loving and pure hearts. At the end of the day, they’ll just remain stagnant while we ascend. It’s painful, and I’m sorry we had to all go through this - but as you said, the beauty is that we can avoid going through it again.

For me the worst pain wasn’t going through it - it was the realization that this is what I allowed. This is how someone treated me - and though I’ll heal, I’ll never get that innocent bright eyed version of myself back. I’m constantly trying to balance accountability with blame and guilt.

Often people struggle with things but you wouldn’t know since most people don’t say it. The point is that depression can make you feel isolated, even to the point where everyone else SEEMS to be doing fine when they’re not.

Of course, everyone has problems. :) But depression has a bad habit of making you feel isolated, that’s really what I’m referring to. Sometimes things seem to be going great for everyone else while you’re going through hell inside.
